transcript.content: Hi, I’m glad you came in today. What brings you in?

Um… I guess what finally pushed me to come in is work stuff. I’m a camera operator and editor, and I’ve been making these technical mistakes that I really do know better than to make. Like labeling camera cards wrong, missing a timecode note, or exporting a client cut with the wrong lower-third even after I thought I checked it.

It sounds small when I say it out loud, but it’s been happening enough that it scared me a little. I don’t want people thinking I’m careless, because I’m really trying not to be.
Have you had trouble paying attention for as long as you can remember, even before this work issue started?

Yeah… I mean, I think so. I don’t want to make it sound like I was a “bad kid” or anything, because I really wasn’t trying to be disruptive, but even in elementary school teachers would move my desk around because I was out of my seat a lot, or I’d blurt out answers before thinking.

Sometimes I’d bother classmates, too, like talking to them or interrupting, and then only realize afterward that I was doing it. So… yes, it probably goes back pretty far, if that answers it.
When you’re working, do you often find your mind drifting away from the task even when you’re trying to focus?

I’m not totally sure how to answer that. I mean, sometimes, sure, my mind wanders a bit, but I don’t know if it’s more than what happens to other people.

At work I’m usually trying really hard to stay with the task, especially because mistakes matter, so I don’t want to overstate it. It’s more that I notice afterward that something slipped by me, if that makes sense. Is that the kind of thing you mean?
Do you find yourself repeatedly checking your work because you can’t shake the feeling that something might be wrong?

I don’t know if I’d say I can’t shake it, exactly. I do check things, but I think that’s also kind of normal for the work, you know? Like you’re supposed to review exports and labels and all that.

Sometimes I’ll go back over something because I’m not fully confident I caught everything, but I’m not sure it’s a repeated-checking thing in the way you mean. Does that answer it okay?
Outside of work mistakes, do you find yourself worrying a lot about many different parts of your life?

I don’t think so? I mean, I worry about normal things—money, family stuff, whether I’m doing okay—but I wouldn’t say it’s across everything all the time.

The work mistakes are the thing that’s been more on my mind. Outside of that, I’m not sure I’d describe myself as someone who’s constantly worrying. Does that make sense?
Do these kinds of attention or follow-through problems also cause trouble for you outside of work?

I’m not really sure. I mean, at home there are little things, like anyone has, where I don’t get to something right away or I forget what I was about to do, but I don’t know that I’d call it “trouble,” exactly.

Work is where I notice it more because there’s more pressure and it’s easier to see when something goes wrong. Outside of work, I guess I’ve kind of adapted around it, or I just don’t track it as much. Is that helpful, or are you asking about specific situations?
Have you been feeling down or depressed lately?

Not really, I don’t think so. I mean, I have days where I feel frustrated or kind of worn out, but I wouldn’t say I’ve been depressed.

I’m functioning okay overall, I think. Maybe a little stressed, but not down in that bigger way—if that’s what you mean?
In your day-to-day life outside of work, do you often have trouble finishing ordinary tasks?

I don’t know if I’d say “often,” exactly. I mean, I do sometimes leave things half-done around the house, but I kind of feel like everyone does that.

Like I’ll start tidying or doing laundry and then something else comes up, and I get back to it later… usually. It doesn’t feel as obvious to me as at work. But maybe I’m undercounting it? What would count as “trouble” in that sense?
Do you often miss appointments or forget plans in your personal life?

I don’t think so? I mean, I use my phone calendar a lot, so that helps. I’m not someone who’s constantly missing things, at least I don’t think I am.

There have probably been times where I’ve almost forgotten something or had to double-check, but I can’t think of a big pattern. Does that answer it the way you mean?
Did these mistakes at work start after a particular stressful event or change?

I think it did line up with a change at work, yeah. It wasn’t like one dramatic event exactly, but after the company readjustment, the way my shoots and edit reviews were run changed, and that’s when the mistakes started being more… noticeable, I guess.

It’s been at that more disruptive level for about two years—maybe two years and a couple months. Does that make sense?
Have these attention problems caused clear difficulties in any part of your life other than work?

I’m not sure I can point to anything really clear outside of work. I mean, day-to-day there are little things, but I don’t know that they’ve caused major problems or anything I’d confidently call “difficulties.”

At home I sort of manage around it, I guess, or it’s less visible. Work is where it’s been most obvious and where other people notice. Is that the kind of distinction you mean?
Have these problems at work been causing you a lot of distress?

Yeah… I mean, I try not to make it into a bigger thing than it is, because I can still do good camera work. But it has been upsetting.

The part that gets to me is that I can tell some producers trust me less now on more complex shoots. They’ll double-check things or give those assignments to someone else, and I understand why, but it feels awful. And I had been hoping to move toward a senior director of photography role, and it feels like that’s kind of slipping away even though the actual quality of my camera work is still strong.

So… yes, I guess it’s causing distress. I don’t know if I’m explaining that the right way.
Since the changes at work, have you felt noticeably more anxious or on edge?

I don’t think so… not in a really noticeable way. I mean, I care more about not messing up, so I can get tense around certain shoots or reviews, but I wouldn’t say I’m generally more anxious or on edge since then.

Unless you mean something more specific by “on edge”? I just don’t want to overstate it.
Have your attention problems ever caused clear problems in your relationships?

Not that I can clearly think of, no. I mean, I’m sure I can be frustrating sometimes, like anyone, but I don’t think my attention issues have caused major relationship problems.

At least… no one close to me has sat me down and said that’s a serious issue. So I’d say not clearly, unless I’m missing something you’re asking about specifically.
Before these work issues, did your attention problems ever clearly cause trouble for you in school?

Yeah… I guess it did, even pretty early on. I don’t want to make it sound like I was some terrible kid, because I wasn’t trying to be disruptive, but in elementary school my teachers would move my desk around because I was out of my seat a lot, or I’d blurt out answers, or I’d bother other kids before I even realized I was doing it.

So… yes, I think it did cause trouble in school, at least in that way.
At home, do your attention problems cause clear difficulties?

At home… I don’t think there are clear difficulties, at least not ones I’d confidently point to. I mean, I’m sure I have moments where I’m not as focused as I should be, but it hasn’t felt like a major problem at home.

If there’s a specific kind of difficulty you mean, I can think about that, but my first answer would be no, not clearly.
Have these attention problems ever clearly interfered with managing your daily life outside of work?

I don’t think so… not clearly. I mean, day-to-day life can feel busy and I probably have the usual moments where I’m a little scattered, but I wouldn’t want to say it’s really interfered unless I’m sure.

So outside of work, I haven’t noticed a clear pattern of it causing major problems. Does that answer what you mean?
When you’re doing something at home that really needs sustained attention, do you often make careless mistakes?

At home specifically… I’m trying to think. It’s not as obvious to me there as it is with work-type tasks.

What scared me enough to come in is more that I’m making these dumb technical mistakes I really should know better than to make — like labeling camera cards wrong, missing a timecode note, or even exporting a client cut with the wrong lower-third after I thought I’d checked it. Which is embarrassing to admit, because it feels so basic.

So if you mean sustained attention in general, yes, I do make careless mistakes. At home, I’m not sure I’d say it shows up as clearly.
When you’re doing something for fun that still requires focus, do you have trouble staying with it?

I’m not sure I’ve really noticed that, honestly. If it’s something I’m doing for fun, I usually either stay with it because I want to, or I just stop and don’t think of it as a problem.

So… I wouldn’t say I clearly have trouble staying with fun things that require focus. At least nothing comes to mind right away. Is that the kind of thing you mean?
Outside of work and school, have these attention problems ever clearly caused problems in any other part of your life?

I’m not sure I can point to something clear outside of work or school. I don’t want to overstate it.

I mean, everyone has little moments where they forget things or get distracted, but I haven’t noticed a definite pattern where attention problems are causing real issues in another part of my life. If there’s a specific area you mean, I can think about it, but nothing obvious is coming to mind.

I’m not sure I can point to something clear outside of work or school. I don’t want to overstate it.

I mean, everyone has little moments where they forget things or get distracted, but I haven’t noticed a definite pattern where attention problems are causing real issues in another part of my life. If there’s a specific area you mean, I can think about it, but nothing obvious is coming to mind.

opening_question.intent: Learn the patient's main reason for seeking help today
opening_question.question: Hi, I’m glad you came in today. What brings you in?

final_diagnosis.reason: Childhood symptoms suggest possible ADHD, but the interview does not establish the full adult syndrome because current symptoms are limited and functional impairment is clearly confirmed only in the occupational setting, not across multiple settings. The most supported formulation is an occupational problem related to work stress/change and distress about job performance.
